control_text: Interactive users must be uniquely attributable wherever technically feasible.
Supported Orion components must use the approved enterprise directory for workforce authentication.
Access must be provisioned through an authorized request and role assignment process.
Access to the Orion platform must be periodically reviewed by an accountable system owner.
Shared interactive identities may only be used where justified and must have compensating controls.
Credentials for shared interactive identities must be protected, rotated and access-controlled.
Non-personal service identities must be limited to automated functions and documented.
Privileged administration must use controlled administrative identities or equivalent safeguards.
Privileged credentials must be centrally governed or otherwise strongly controlled.
Remote administrative access must use an approved brokered path and strong authentication.
Remote administrative access must use multi-factor authentication when applicable.
The Orion platform must be placed on a segregated manufacturing network with restricted routing.
Inbound and outbound flows must be limited to documented business and support requirements.
Direct Internet connectivity from Orion components must not be permitted.
Security-relevant events from supported Orion components must be forwarded to central monitoring.
Components unable to forward events centrally must retain sufficient local audit information.
System time must be synchronized to an approved enterprise time source where supported.
Supported server and workstation components must receive security patches through a controlled process.
Industrial components requiring vendor validation must have a documented local patch process.
The Orion environment must be included in vulnerability identification activities where technically safe.
Malware protection must be enabled on supported general-purpose operating systems.
Application execution restrictions should be used on engineering endpoints where compatible.
Critical Orion server data and configuration must be backed up at an approved frequency.
Backup restoration must be periodically tested and evidence retained.
A recovery plan must define restoration of Orion services following a disruptive event.
Recovery procedures must be exercised periodically or during an equivalent controlled test.
Supplier support access must be explicitly approved, time-bounded and attributable.
Supplier remote sessions must use the approved remote administration path when enabled.
Production records transferred from Orion to central systems must be protected from unauthorized modification.
Configuration changes affecting production must be authorized and traceable.
Removable media use on Orion components must be restricted and controlled.
Physical access to Orion control and engineering components must be restricted to authorized personnel.
